title: Printable parallel-lines worksheet (lesson 54)
subject: Mathematics
source: Seeded from mathematics/y8 lesson 54 (Printable parallel-lines worksheet (portal worksheet for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 54: Angles in parallel lines: corresponding and alternate. To understand why corresponding and alternate angles in parallel lines are equal and use them to find missing angles

model.title: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. Above the first line, on the right, the angle is 70°. Find the angle in the same position at the second line.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Same position at each crossing: corresponding angles

model.title: Between the parallel lines, an angle on the left of the transversal is 125°. Find the alternate angle.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Between the lines, on opposite sides of the transversal: alternate angles

questions.q: Find the angle alternate to 72° and the angle next to that one on the same straight line.
questions.model: Alternate angles are equal: 72°. Angles on a straight line add up to 180°: 180 - 72 = 108°.

questions.q: Which angles make an F shape?
Two lines are crossed by a transversal. The corresponding angles are 64° and 66°. Are the lines parallel?
questions.a: No: in parallel lines corresponding angles are equal.

questions.q: Find each lettered angle with a reason: (a) a corresponds to 57° (b) b is alternate to 131° (c) c lies on a straight line with an angle that corresponds to 75° (d) d is vertically opposite an angle that is alternate to 44°
questions.model: (c) The corresponding angle is 75° (corresponding angles are equal). c = 180 - 75 = 105° (angles on a straight line add up to 180°).

questions.q: Angles (3x + 10)° and (5x - 30)° are alternate angles. Find x and the angle.
questions.a: 3x + 10 = 5x - 30, so x = 20 and the angle is 70°

questions.q: Use parallel-line facts to explain why neighbouring angles of a parallelogram add up to 180°.
questions.a: Extend one side: one angle and the corresponding angle lie on a straight line with the neighbour, so they add up to 180°.

questions.q: An F shape shows which angles?
Big question: why do so many angles turn out equal?
questions.a: The transversal crosses both parallel lines at the same angle, so the angles at each crossing match (corresponding and alternate angles).
